full_judgment: 2. The Opposite Party Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 37 of 1979 in the court of the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong impleading the Petitioner and Opposite Party Nos. 3 to 6 as defendants praying for a decree of recovery of khas possession of the suit land described in the schedule of the plaint on declaration of the plaintiffs' title thereto. The plaint case is that the suit land originally belonged to One Ramzan Ali who passed away leaving two sons, Abdul Wahab alias Thanda Miah and Gura Miah as heirs. Gura Miah passed away leaving one son Md. Yusuf and Thanda Miah passed away leaving his only son Fazlul Haque as their respective heirs. Md. Yusuf sold his share of the suit land to Fazlul Haque by a deed of sale dated 19.6.1978 and thus Fazlul Haque became the sole owner of the entire suit property. It is asserted, accordingly, that the R.S. and P.S. Khatians in respect of the suit land were correctly prepared in Fazlul Haque's name who by four deeds of sale dated 20.7.1978, 24.7.1978, 27.7.1978 and 28.7.1978 transferred eight gandas out of the suit land to the plaintiffs who consequently mutated the land in their favour and Mutation Khatian No. 285/1 was opened in their names. It is also asserted that prior to such purchase the plaintiffs had caused to have published a notice in a daily newspaper pursuant and in response to which no claims were raised upon the suit land. It having so transpired that on 25.12.1978 the defendants having forcibly dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land and resorted to barbed wire fencing of the suit land and the plaintiffs' numerous requests thereafter for a restoration of possession being of no avail, the latter were therefore compelled to institute the suit.
